title: Gabriel, cardinal de Gramont, Rome, to Montmorency, 21 July 1530, BnF fr. 3071 no. 7 f. 17 (catalogue item 6, Gramont's cipher 1530)

plaintext.source: No decipherment found. Lasry decoded the text in 2023, unpublished.

transcription.notes: 14 cipher lines (NOTES); no glyph-alias file kept.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on graphic signs, two to seven homophones per letter, LL/RR/SS signs, COM and CON signs, a few code signs and nulls ('Gramont's cipher (1530)', Lasry's table for fr. 3071 f. 17; Tomokiyo's sibling fr. 3019 f. 20).
system.sibling_key: Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' (GL.htm, GL/BnF_fr3071_f17.png; copy img/BnF_fr3071_f17.png); Tomokiyo's table from fr. 3019 f. 20 (img/francisGramont.png).
system.notes: Lasry's table lists five unknown signs; three identified here from context: 8Δ = pape, key-ring sign = roy, ʃʃ on a stem = word-initial null. g serves B, V and E. Homophone maxima counted from Lasry's table as transcribed in fr3071_no7_gramont.md (R has 7 forms incl. ligatures; O has 4).

prior_solution.where: Key published online by Lasry (table dated 4-5 Nov 2023 on cryptiana GL.htm). Lasry also decoded this letter in 2023, unpublished (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue item; no target-specific intervention recorded. Relayed Lasry's 21 Sept 2026 correction on his unpublished decipherments.

solution.what: Matched the four items against Tomokiyo's francis.htm and GL.htm: four letters, four different keys, all tabulated by Lasry in 2023; no plaintext on either site.
Located the correct Gallica arks (fr. 3091 is btv1b9060253s, not the catalogue's) and fetched full-resolution canvases.
Applied Lasry's 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' table to the 14 cipher lines of f. 17r by eye from line strips.
Read about 85 % of the cipher; identified three of Lasry's five unknown signs (8Δ = pape, key-ring = roy, ʃʃ-on-stem null). Ends of lines 1-2 and the middle of lines 5-7 at lower confidence.
Dated to 21 July 1530 by the return of the Queen and the princes (Bidassoa, 1 July 1530) and Rodolfo Pio's mission as nuncio.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded all four texts in 2023 when reconstructing the keys, but the decipherments were never published. Prior-solution record updated: a reading existed, unpublished, learned of after the reading and not used (only his keys were).

Split the combined catalogue item 6 entry under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): four letters in four keys. gramont1529 keeps fr. 3091 no. 23 (Gramont's cipher 1529); langeac1529 takes fr. 3083 no. 8 (Avranches' cipher 1); gramont1530 takes fr. 3071 no. 7 (Gramont's cipher 1530); the Mâcon letter fr. 3071 no. 4 moved to rome1536 with the other letters in Mascon's cipher. This entry is fr3071_no7_gramont.md, moved from targets/gramont1529/.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Lasry's 2023 table 'Gramont's cipher (1530)' for this letter (cryptiana GL.htm); no new cryptanalysis.
outcome.fraction_read_source: fr3071_no7_gramont.md: 'about 85 % of the cipher is read' (ends of lines 1-2 and the middle of lines 5-7 lower confidence). No alias file kept, so not counted.

gaps.item: ends of cipher lines 1-2 and the middle of lines 5-7 (about 15 % of the cipher)
gaps.detail: the stretches carry signs Lasry's table leaves unknown (the grid sign, the crown) and the ambiguous g (B/V/E); no gloss, clear copy or decipherment of this letter exists

gaps.item: two of Lasry's five unknown signs (crown, ꝛ-bar or ꟿ) without a value
gaps.detail: each occurs too rarely here to fix from context

outcome.notes: About 85 % read: the Pope keeps Francisque on the mission instead of Gramont; Rodolfo Pio, bishop of Faenza, to congratulate the King on the return of the Queen and the princes.
